item.title: IRN-BRU — A.G. Barr
item.description: Secret-recipe carbonated soda made with 32 flavours, launched in 1901. A Scottish staple with no regular US grocery distribution; US buyers need import/specialty channels. Made by A.G. Barr.

item.title: Moxie — Coca-Cola-owned Moxie brand
item.description: Gentian-root soda; Maine's official soft drink since 2005, also sold in cane-sugar glass bottles. Distribution is rooted in New England, with only spotty availability elsewhere in the US. Made by Coca-Cola-owned Moxie brand.

item.title: Milkis — Lotte Chilsung Beverage
item.description: Milk-and-yogurt cream soda in 250ml cans, sold since 1989. A Korean soda category with no equivalent in regular US grocery distribution. Made by Lotte Chilsung Beverage.

item.title: Inca Kola — Corporación José R. Lindley S.A.
item.description: Golden, lemon-verbena-flavored kola sold since 1935. Peru's flagship soda; the original Peruvian version is an import/specialty find in the US. Made by Corporación José R. Lindley S.A. (part of Coca-Cola).

item.title: Vernors Ginger Soda — Vernors brand (Keurig Dr Pepper)
item.description: Ginger soda created in 1866 and billed as the oldest soda in the US; a Michigan favorite, with a current zero-sugar bottle listing verifying ongoing sale. Distribution and cultural footprint are centered on Michigan and the Great Lakes region. Made by Vernors brand (Keurig Dr Pepper).

item.title: Guaraná Antarctica — Ambev
item.description: Guaraná-berry soda sold since 1921. Brazil's signature guaraná soda is not part of regular US grocery distribution. Made by Ambev.

item.title: Sidral Mundet — Coca-Cola FEMSA (US distribution via Novamex)
item.description: Apple soda sold since 1902, known for its signature 12oz glass bottles; a Zero variant launched in September 2026. The glass-bottle Mexican original is a specialty/import buy rather than a regular US grocery item. Made by Coca-Cola FEMSA (US distribution via Novamex).

item.title: Calpis Soda — Calpis Co., Ltd. (Asahi)
item.description: Carbonated version of the Calpis fermented-milk drink — light, milky, and slightly acidic — sold in cans and bottles in Japan. The carbonated Japanese version is distinct from the still drinks sold under the brand in North America and requires import channels. Made by Calpis Co., Ltd. (Asahi).

item.title: Mitsuya Cider — Asahi Soft Drinks
item.description: Clear carbonated "cider" with a lemon-lime/ginger-ale-cross flavor, created in 1884. A Japan-market staple since the 1800s with no regular US grocery distribution. Made by Asahi Soft Drinks.

item.title: Orangina — Suntory
item.description: Lightly carbonated soda made with 12% citrus juice and 2% orange pulp, introduced in 1936 and sold in an iconic round bottle. The French pulp-in formula and bottle format reach US buyers through importers, not regular grocery sets. Made by Suntory.

item.title: Ting — D&G (Desnoes & Geddes)
item.description: Grapefruit soda made from real Jamaican grapefruit, sold since 1976. A Jamaican-market soda that reaches US buyers only through Caribbean/import specialty sellers. Made by D&G (Desnoes & Geddes) (part of Heineken).

item.title: Bundaberg Ginger Beer — Bundaberg Brewed Drinks
item.description: Craft-brewed over 3 days, sold in a 375ml glass bottle with a rip-cap. An Australian brewed soda that reaches the US only through import/specialty channels, not regular grocery sets. Made by Bundaberg Brewed Drinks.

item.title: Sangaria Ramune — Sangaria
item.description: Codd-neck marble-sealed glass bottle, 6.76 fl oz, sold in multiple flavors. The Japanese marble-bottle format is an import-shop item in the US, not a grocery staple. Made by Sangaria.

item.title: Kinnie — Simonds Farsons Cisk
item.description: Bittersweet carbonated soda brewed from bitter oranges and wormwood extracts, sold since 1952 in glass bottles, cans, and PET. Malta's national soft drink, produced in Malta and exported only as a specialty item — no regular US grocery distribution. Made by Simonds Farsons Cisk.

item.title: Fanta Melon — Fanta
item.description: Sweet green melon soda, a Japanese convenience-store and vending-machine staple, sold in 250ml cans and PET bottles. A Japan-market Fanta flavor never released in US grocery distribution; US buyers need Japanese import shops. Made by Fanta (part of Coca-Cola).

item.title: Fanta Shokata — Fanta
item.description: Elderflower-and-lemon soda inspired by socată, the traditional Romanian elderflower drink, sold in 0.5L bottles and cans. A regional European Fanta flavor with no US release; US buyers find it only via Balkan/European import grocers. Made by Fanta (part of Coca-Cola).

item.title: Solo Original Lemon — Solo
item.description: Lemon "pub squash"-style carbonated soft drink made with crushed lemon, sold in 375ml cans and bottles since the 1970s. An Australian-market brand sold only in Australia (and New Zealand channels); not part of US grocery distribution. Made by Solo (part of Asahi).

item.title: Sanpellegrino Chinotto — Sanpellegrino Italian Sparkling Drinks
item.description: Dark, bittersweet sparkling soda made from chinotto (myrtle-leaved orange) extract and a blend of herbs, sold in 330ml cans since the 1950s. An Italian cult drink consumed mainly in Italy and Malta; in the US it surfaces only in Italian delis and specialty import shops, not regular grocery sets. Made by Sanpellegrino Italian Sparkling Drinks (part of Nestlé).

item.title: Barr Bubblegum Soda — Barr
item.description: Bright-blue, bubblegum-flavored sparkling soft drink from AG Barr's long-running UK Barr flavours range, sold in 330ml cans and 500ml bottles. A UK-market soda with no US grocery distribution; US buyers find it only through British import shops. Made by Barr (part of A.G. Barr).

item.title: Manzana Postobón — Postobón
item.description: Colombia's iconic pink apple soda — sweet, bright pink, and unmistakably Postobón Manzana Postobón is a Colombian national icon; outside Latin import shops it has no US distribution. Made by Postobón.

item.title: Lucozade Energy Original — Lucozade
item.description: The original sparkling glucose energy drink, sold in the UK since 1927 Lucozade is a UK institution now under Suntory; the original is a British shelf staple that US grocery stores do not stock. Made by Lucozade (part of Suntory).

item.title: Club Orange — Britvic Ireland
item.description: Ireland's No. 1 orange carbonate — a sparkling orange soda made with real fruit bits in the juice Club Orange is an Irish-market soda from Britvic Ireland; US buyers find it only through Irish import shops. Made by Britvic Ireland.

item.title: Rubicon Sparkling Mango — Rubicon
item.description: Sparkling mango soft drink made with real fruit juice, from AG Barr's Rubicon range Rubicon's sparkling cans are a UK-market line from AG Barr with no regular US grocery distribution. Made by Rubicon (part of A.G. Barr).

item.title: Fanta White Peach (Japan) — Fanta
item.description: White peach Fanta made by Coca-Cola Japan as a flavor for the Japanese market A Japan-market Fanta flavor; white peach is sold in Japan and reaches the US only through importers. Made by Fanta (part of Coca-Cola).

item.title: Barr Tizer — Barr
item.description: A red, mixed-fruit sparkling soda from AG Barr, on Scottish shelves since 1924 Tizer is a UK-market AG Barr soda with no US grocery distribution; US buyers find it only through British import shops. Made by Barr (part of A.G. Barr).

item.title: Kit Kat Rich Matcha — Nestlé Japan
item.description: Bag of 10 individually wrapped mini wafer bars in rich matcha chocolate. Japan-market Kit Kat flavor program; this rich-matcha edition is not part of the US Kit Kat lineup. Made by Nestlé Japan.

item.title: Coffee Crisp — Nestlé Canada
item.description: 50 g bar of alternating coffee-crème and wafer layers in milk chocolate. A Canada-only Nestlé bar in continuous production since the 1930s; no US grocery distribution. Made by Nestlé Canada.

item.title: Big Turk — Nestlé Canada
item.description: 60 g bar of magenta Turkish-delight jelly coated in milk chocolate. Manufactured by Nestlé in Canada for the Canadian market only; no equivalent bar exists in the US Nestlé range. Made by Nestlé Canada.

item.title: Smarties — Nestlé Canada
item.description: 45 g box of candy-coated milk chocolate pieces, made in a peanut-free facility. The name collides with the US tablet candy — the chocolate Smarties are a Canadian (and overseas) product with no US grocery sale. Made by Nestlé Canada.

item.title: Aero S'Mores — Nestlé Canada
item.description: 42 g aerated milk chocolate bar in a s'mores flavor edition, flagged "limited time" on Nestlé Canada's official site. A time-boxed Canadian flavor edition of a bar the US doesn't carry in this form; gone when the run ends. Made by Nestlé Canada.

item.title: Kit Kat Chunky Peanut Butter — Kit Kat
item.description: Multipack of four 34 g chunky single-finger wafer bars with a creamed peanut topping covered in milk chocolate. The Chunky format and this peanut butter edition are Nestlé UK lines; the US Kit Kat range (made under license by a different company) has never included a Chunky Peanut Butter bar in grocery distribution. Made by Kit Kat (part of Nestlé).

item.title: Hi-Chew Shikuwasa — Morinaga
item.description: 5-stick pack (310 g) of chewy fruit candy made with Okinawan shikuwasa citrus juice. A regional limited edition sold for the Okinawa market — even within Japan it is a souvenir item, and the flavor is not in the US Hi-Chew range. Made by Morinaga.

item.title: Kororo Muscat Grape Gummy — UHA Mikakuto
item.description: 40 g pouch of muscat grape gummies made with 100% fruit juice, with a thin skin-like membrane for a fresh-fruit bite. Japanese domestic gummy line with no regular US grocery distribution; muscat grape is a Japan-market flavor. Made by UHA Mikakuto.

item.title: Alfort Mini Chocolate — Bourbon
item.description: 59 g box of 12 mini whole-wheat biscuits topped with a milk chocolate slab stamped with a sailboat design. A Japanese household staple biscuit-chocolate that Bourbon sells for its home market; reaches the US only through importers. Made by Bourbon.

item.title: Apollo Strawberry Chocolate — Meiji
item.description: 46 g box of bite-size cone-shaped chocolates — strawberry chocolate tip over a milk chocolate base. One of Meiji's signature Japanese confections since 1969; Meiji's US presence is a different, narrow product range and Apollo is not in US grocery distribution. Made by Meiji.

item.title: Kinoko no Yama — Kinoko no Yama (Meiji)
item.description: 74 g box of mushroom-shaped biscuits — crunchy biscuit stems topped with milk chocolate caps. One of Meiji's signature Japanese confections since 1975; the original Japanese product is not in US grocery distribution (Meiji's US arm markets a separately rebranded cousin instead), so it reaches US buyers only through importers. Made by Kinoko no Yama (Meiji).

item.title: Eat-More — Hershey Canada
item.description: 52 g chewy bar of dark toffee, roasted peanuts, and chocolate. A Hershey product made only for Canada — the same parent company sells nothing like it in its US bar lineup. Made by Hershey Canada.

item.title: Crunchie — Cadbury (Mondelez UK)
item.description: Milk chocolate bar with a golden honeycomb (sponge toffee) centre. A UK Cadbury staple since 1929 that Cadbury has never put into US grocery distribution. Made by Cadbury (Mondelez UK).

item.title: Wispa — Cadbury (Mondelez UK)
item.description: 36 g bar of aerated milk chocolate — intensely bubbled chocolate under a smooth chocolate layer. UK-only Cadbury bar (famously revived by a fan campaign); US Cadbury licensed production does not include it. Made by Cadbury (Mondelez UK).

item.title: Maynards Bassetts Jelly Babies — Maynards Bassetts (Mondelez UK)
item.description: 130 g sharing bag of soft fruit jelly sweets in six named baby characters/flavors. A British classic dating to the 19th century, sold for the UK market; no US grocery distribution. Made by Maynards Bassetts (Mondelez UK).

item.title: Cherry Ripe — Cadbury Australia (Mondelez)
item.description: 52 g bar of cherries and coconut coated in Old Gold dark chocolate. Australia's oldest chocolate bar, sold only in AU/NZ markets; Cadbury does not export it to US grocery. Made by Cadbury Australia (Mondelez).

item.title: Caramello Koala — Cadbury Australia (Mondelez)
item.description: 35 g koala-shaped Dairy Milk chocolate with a flowing caramel centre. A character bar made for the Australian market for three generations; never sold in US grocery. Made by Cadbury Australia (Mondelez).

item.title: Cadbury Dairy Milk Top Deck — Cadbury
item.description: 150 g slab of Dairy Milk milk chocolate topped with a layer of white chocolate on every block. Top Deck is a signature slab of Cadbury's South African range (also sold in Australia); Mondelez does not sell it in the US, where the Cadbury name is licensed out for a narrow, different bar lineup. Made by Cadbury (part of Mondelez).

item.title: Duvalín Bi Sabor — Ricolino
item.description: 18-pack of small cups of spoonable two-flavor candy cream (strawberry and vanilla), each with a mini spoon. One of Mexico's most iconic candies, sold through Mexican specialty importers rather than US grocery candy aisles. Made by Ricolino (part of Mondelez).

item.title: MAOAM Kracher — Haribo (MAOAM)
item.description: 200 g bag of sugar-coated chewy dragees with a fizzy sherbet filling, in strawberry, raspberry, apple, orange, lemon, and cola. Haribo's German MAOAM line is a home-market range; the US Haribo catalog is built around Goldbears and does not include Kracher. Made by Haribo (MAOAM).

item.title: Haribo Tangfastics — Haribo
item.description: 175 g sharing bag of fizzy fruit- and cola-flavour gums plus sweet foam gums (cherries, cola bottles, crocodiles) with a sour sugar coating. Tangfastics is a flagship line of Haribo's UK range, launched there in 1997; the US Haribo catalog is built around Goldbears and does not carry Tangfastics in grocery distribution. Made by Haribo.

item.title: Galaxy Minstrels — Galaxy
item.description: 195 g sharing pouch of Galaxy milk chocolate buttons (75% milk chocolate) in a crisp sugar shell. Minstrels are a UK Galaxy line with no US equivalent; Mars sells its chocolate under the Dove name in the US and has never put Minstrels into US grocery distribution. Made by Galaxy (part of Mars).

item.title: Kinder Happy Hippo — Kinder
item.description: Box of five individually wrapped 20.7 g hippo-shaped wafer biscuits with a double cream filling of milk and cocoa creams. A long-running Ferrero line in Europe since the 1980s, but Ferrero's US Kinder range is built on other products — Happy Hippo reaches the US only through importers, never grocery shelves. Made by Kinder (part of Ferrero).

item.title: Cadbury Mini Eggs — Cadbury (Mondelez UK)
item.description: Solid milk chocolate eggs in crisp pastel sugar shells — Cadbury's Easter-season classic Mini Eggs in the UK pack from Mondelez UK appear only for the Easter season; the rest of the year they are gone from shelves. Made by Cadbury (Mondelez UK).

item.title: Milka Oreo Sandwich — Milka
item.description: Alpine milk chocolate bar sandwiching mini Oreos in a vanilla cream filling, made in Bremen A European Milka bar made in Germany; this Oreo sandwich format is sold across Europe but not in US grocery. Made by Milka (part of Mondelez).

item.title: Calbee Pizza Potato — Calbee
item.description: Potato chips with pizza-style cheese and tomato seasoning, a long-running Japanese Calbee line. Japan-market flavor edition; US Calbee distribution does not carry this line in regular grocery. Made by Calbee.

item.title: Haitai Honey Butter Chips — Haitai-Calbee
item.description: Thin potato chips with a sweet honey-butter seasoning. Korean-market product; the honey butter chip format originated in Korea and is not a US grocery staple. Made by Haitai-Calbee (part of Haitai Confectionery).

item.title: Lay's Ketchup Chips — Frito-Lay Canada
item.description: Ketchup-flavoured potato chips, a signature Canadian Lay's flavor. Ketchup chips are a Canada-only Lay's edition, not sold by US Frito-Lay in grocery stores. Made by Frito-Lay Canada (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Walkers Prawn Cocktail — Walkers
item.description: Potato crisps with tangy prawn cocktail seasoning, sold here in a 45g grab bag. Prawn cocktail is a classic British crisp flavor that US chip aisles do not carry. Made by Walkers (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Lay's Cucumber Flavor — Lay's (China)
item.description: Potato chips with a cool cucumber flavor, an edition made for the Chinese market. China-exclusive Lay's flavor; US Lay's has never released a cucumber edition. Made by Lay's (China) (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: McCoy's Flame Grilled Steak — KP Snacks
item.description: Thick ridged potato crisps with flame grilled steak seasoning, 45g grab bag. McCoy's is a UK brand with no US grocery presence; steak is one of its core UK flavors. Made by KP Snacks (part of Intersnack).

item.title: Monster Munch Pickled Onion — Walkers
item.description: Baked corn snack in a monster-paw shape with pickled onion flavor. A British lunchbox staple format and flavor combination not produced for the US market. Made by Walkers (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Ruffles Sour Cream 'n Bacon — Frito-Lay Canada
item.description: Ridged potato chips with sour cream and bacon flavoring, a Canadian Ruffles edition. This Ruffles flavor pairing is sold in Canada and is not part of the US Ruffles lineup. Made by Frito-Lay Canada (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Sabritas Adobadas — Sabritas
item.description: Potato chips with adobada seasoning — a tangy, chile-and-tomato style coating. Sabritas is PepsiCo's Mexican brand; its Adobadas edition is made for the Mexican market only. Made by Sabritas (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Lay's Patatje Joppie — Lay's / PepsiCo Nederland
item.description: Potato chips flavored after Dutch Joppiesaus, the curry-mayo fry sauce. A Netherlands-only Lay's edition built on a Dutch fry-shop sauce with no US equivalent release. Made by Lay's / PepsiCo Nederland.

item.title: Pringles Prawn Cocktail — Pringles (Kellanova)
item.description: Stackable potato crisps in a resealable tube with prawn cocktail seasoning, 185g UK sharing size. Prawn cocktail is a UK-only Pringles flavor; the US Pringles range does not include it. Made by Pringles (Kellanova).

item.title: Smith's Crinkle Cut Chicken — Smith's
item.description: Crinkle-cut potato chips with chicken seasoning; introduced in 1961 as Australia's first flavored chip. Smith's is Australia's home-market chip brand; chicken-flavored chips are an Australian staple not sold in US grocery. Made by Smith's (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Ruffles Queso — Sabritas
item.description: Ridged potato chips with an intense queso cheese seasoning made for the Mexican market. The Sabritas-made Mexican Ruffles Queso recipe differs from US Ruffles and is sold only in Mexico. Made by Sabritas (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Calbee Jagabee Soy Sauce & Butter — Calbee
item.description: Crunchy potato sticks seasoned with butter and soy sauce powder, 85g bag. Jagabee is Calbee's Japan-market potato stick line in a butter–soy sauce flavor not released in the US. Made by Calbee.

item.title: Tim's Cascade Jalapeño — Tim's Cascade Snacks (Utz)
item.description: Extra-crunchy cascade-style potato chips with jalapeño seasoning; stocked at PNW grocery chains such as QFC. A brand built on its Pacific Northwest identity since 1986, with retail weight in that region. Made by Tim's Cascade Snacks (Utz).

item.title: Lay's India's Magic Masala — PepsiCo India
item.description: Potato chips seasoned with a masala spice blend (cumin, coriander, chili, onion, garlic); a flagship flavor of Lay's Indian lineup. Made by PepsiCo India for the Indian market only; US Frito-Lay has never released a masala edition in grocery. Made by PepsiCo India.

item.title: funny-frisch Chipsfrisch Ungarisch — funny-frisch (Intersnack)
item.description: Thin potato chips cooked in sunflower oil with a smoky Hungarian paprika seasoning, 150g bag. A German supermarket staple from Intersnack's funny-frisch brand, which has no regular US grocery distribution. Made by funny-frisch (Intersnack).

item.title: Chitato Potato Chips — Indofood
item.description: Potato chips with grilled beef barbecue (sapi panggang) seasoning, 68g bag; Chitato is Indofood's flagship chip brand. Indonesia's market-leading chip brand, sold across Indonesian retail with no US grocery distribution. Made by Indofood.

item.title: Walkers Cheese & Onion — Walkers
item.description: Potato crisps with cheese and onion seasoning, sold here in a 45g grab bag; one of Walkers' core UK flavors. Cheese & onion is a signature British crisp flavor; Walkers' edition is a UK-market product not sold through US grocery (Wave A carried Walkers Prawn Cocktail and Monster Munch — this is a distinct flavor). Made by Walkers (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Lay's Nori Seaweed — Lay's
item.description: Potato chips seasoned with nori seaweed flakes and soy-sauce powder, 48g bag. Thailand-market Lay's flavor; US Frito-Lay has never released a seaweed edition in grocery. Made by Lay's (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Lay's Hot Chili Squid — Lay's
item.description: Thin potato chips with a spicy chili and savory squid seasoning, ~48g bag. A signature Thai Lay's flavor built on seafood seasoning, a profile US Lay's does not sell. Made by Lay's (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Doritos Chilli Heatwave — Doritos (Walkers)
item.description: Corn tortilla chips with a sweet-chili heatwave seasoning, 180g sharing bag. Chilli Heatwave is the UK Doritos flagship flavor; the US Doritos lineup has no equivalent edition. Made by Doritos (Walkers) (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Lay's Receta Campesina — Lay's
item.description: Potato chips with a "country recipe" seasoning of vegetables, onion, paprika, tomato and herbs. Campesina is a Spain-market Lay's flavor with no US counterpart release. Made by Lay's (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Doritos Incógnita — Doritos (Sabritas)
item.description: A Sabritas Mexico Doritos edition with a tangy, spiced seasoning blend, sold in a black bag. A Mexico-market Doritos edition from PepsiCo's Sabritas arm; US Frito-Lay does not sell it, so US buyers find it through Mexican import grocers. Made by Doritos (Sabritas) (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Rancheritos — Rancheritos (Sabritas)
item.description: Nixtamalized corn totopos with chile and spice seasoning, 60g bag; a Sabritas house brand. Rancheritos is a Mexican-market Sabritas brand with no US grocery distribution. Made by Rancheritos (Sabritas) (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Kurkure Masala Munch — Kurkure
item.description: Crunchy twisted corn/rice puffs coated in a tangy masala spice blend; Kurkure is PepsiCo India's homegrown snack brand. Kurkure was created for India and is not distributed through US grocery channels. Made by Kurkure (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Smith's Crinkle Cut Salt & Vinegar — Smith's
item.description: Crinkle-cut potato chips with a tangy salt & vinegar seasoning, up to 380g party bag size. Smith's is PepsiCo's Australia-only chip brand; Wave A carried its Chicken flavor, this is the distinct Salt & Vinegar edition. Made by Smith's (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Tayto Cheese & Onion — Tayto Snacks
item.description: Potato crisps with cheese and onion flavoring, made from Irish-grown potatoes. Tayto is Ireland's original crisp brand, sold in Irish supermarkets, not US ones. Made by Tayto Snacks (part of Tayto Group).

item.title: Pringles Paprika — Pringles
item.description: Stackable crisps in a resealable tube with sweet paprika seasoning, 165g. Paprika is a core European Pringles flavor; the US Pringles range does not include it. Made by Pringles (part of Kellanova).

item.title: Pringles Butter Caramel — Pringles
item.description: Stackable crisps with a sweet butter-caramel (butterscotch) seasoning, 100–110g can. A Korea-exclusive sweet Pringles flavor with no US equivalent release. Made by Pringles (part of Kellanova).

item.title: Calbee Consommé Punch — Calbee
item.description: Potato chips with a chicken-and-beef consommé seasoning and a hint of plum, 55g bag. Consommé Punch is one of Calbee's flagship Japan flavors and is not part of US Calbee grocery distribution. Made by Calbee.

item.title: Calbee Hot & Spicy — Calbee
item.description: Potato chips with a bold chili-heat seasoning, 105g bag; the flagship flavor of Calbee's Hong Kong line. Made for the Hong Kong market by Calbee's local operation; a different product from Japan's Karamucho line (which is Koikeya anyway) and not sold in US grocery. Made by Calbee.

item.title: Wotsits Really Cheesy — Wotsits (Walkers)
item.description: Baked maize puffs with a strong cheese flavor, sold in multipacks and grab bags. Wotsits is a UK lunchbox staple brand with no US production or grocery presence. Made by Wotsits (Walkers) (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Hula Hoops Original — Hula Hoops (KP Snacks)
item.description: Original salted potato rings — crunchy ring-shaped potato snacks, 6x24g multipack. Hula Hoops is a British format/flavor institution under KP Snacks with no US grocery distribution. Made by Hula Hoops (KP Snacks) (part of Intersnack).

item.title: Old Dutch Ketchup Chips — Old Dutch
item.description: Potato chips with a bold, tangy ketchup seasoning, in sizes from 40g vending bags to 255g. Ketchup chips are a Canadian category the US never adopted; Old Dutch's edition is sold across Canada but not in US grocery (Wave A carried the Lay's Canada ketchup edition — this is the competing Canadian house's version). Made by Old Dutch.

item.title: Barcel Chip's Jalapeño — Barcel
item.description: Kettle-style potato chips with jalapeño seasoning from Mexico's Barcel brand. Barcel's Chip's line is a Mexican-market brand not distributed through US grocery. Made by Barcel (part of Grupo Bimbo).

item.title: Koikeya Karamucho Hot Chili — Koikeya
item.description: Hot chili potato chips with garlic umami; Karamucho is Japan's original spicy chip line, sold since 1984. Japan-market line from Koikeya with no regular US grocery distribution. Made by Koikeya.

item.title: Doritos Tangy Cheese — Doritos
item.description: Tangy Cheese flavour corn chips in a 180g sharing bag — the standard Doritos flavour on UK shelves. Tangy Cheese is a UK-market Doritos flavour that US Frito-Lay does not sell in US grocery stores. Made by Doritos (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Zapp's New Orleans Kettle Style Voodoo Potato Chips — Zapp's
item.description: New Orleans kettle-style potato chips dusted with Zapp's sweet-heat Voodoo seasoning Zapp's is a Louisiana kettle-chip brand whose shelf presence leans on the Gulf South and regional channels; most US grocery stores never stock it. Made by Zapp's (part of Utz Brands).

item.title: Utz Chesapeake Bay Crab Potato Chips — Utz
item.description: Potato chips covered in Chesapeake Bay crab seasoning — the Mid-Atlantic's signature spice blend A regional flavor built for the Chesapeake Bay area; Utz's crab chips are a Mid-Atlantic staple that seldom travels beyond the region. Made by Utz (part of Utz Brands).

item.title: Golden Flake Sweet Heat Barbecue Potato Chips — Golden Flake
item.description: Thin, crispy potato chips in a sweet-heat barbecue seasoning from an Alabama heritage brand Golden Flake is an Alabama heritage brand now in the Utz portfolio; its distribution stays concentrated in the Southeast. Made by Golden Flake (part of Utz Brands).

item.title: Orion Turtle Chips Corn Soup — Orion
item.description: Four-layer, turtle-shell-shaped corn chips with a sweet corn soup flavor — Korea's famous layered chip A Korean-market Orion snack sold across Asia; it has no regular US grocery distribution. Made by Orion.

item.title: Bingo! Mad Angles Achaari Masti — Bingo!
item.description: Crunchy triangle crisps seasoned achaari-style — achaari is a tangy Indian pickle-spice blend Bingo! is ITC's Indian snack brand and Mad Angles are an India-market staple; US grocery stores do not carry them. Made by Bingo! (part of ITC Limited).

item.title: Red Rock Deli Sweet Chilli & Sour Cream — Smith's
item.description: Premium deli-style potato chips with sweet chilli and sour cream seasoning, from Smith's Australia Red Rock Deli is Smith's premium Australian line, made for the Australian market; its flavors are not sold in US grocery. Made by Smith's (part of PepsiCo).

item.title: Nik Naks Nice 'n Spicy — KP Snacks
item.description: Knobbly corn snack sticks in a sweet-spicy Nice 'n Spicy coating — a KP Snacks classic since the 1980s Nik Naks are a UK shelf staple with no US grocery distribution; US buyers find them only through British import shops. Made by KP Snacks (part of Intersnack).

item.title: Seabrook Crinkle Cut Canadian Ham — Seabrook
item.description: Crinkle-cut crisps with Canadian ham seasoning from Seabrook, the Yorkshire crisp maker going since 1945 Seabrook is a Yorkshire brand now under Calbee UK; its crisps are sold in the UK and rarely appear in US stores. Made by Seabrook (part of Calbee).

item.title: Koikeya STRONG Rich Pizza — Koikeya
item.description: Potato chips from Koikeya's STRONG line — its rich, 'gachi nōkō' deep-flavor series — loaded with pizza seasoning The STRONG line is a Japan-market Koikeya range; the rich pizza flavor is not sold outside Japan. Made by Koikeya.

item.title: Doritos Mexican Taco Flavor (Japan) — Japan Frito-Lay
item.description: Taco-seasoned Doritos made by Japan Frito-Lay as a market flavor for Japanese shelves A Japan-market Doritos flavor from Calbee's Japan Frito-Lay; this taco edition is not part of the US Doritos lineup. Made by Japan Frito-Lay (part of Calbee).

item.title: Pom-Bär Original — Pom-Bär
